t: Formed on 1 January 1801 by the union of Great Britain and Ireland, with a single Parliament at Westminster.
The first industrial nation, it led world trade and finance and ruled the largest empire in history.
Irish grievances, deepened by the Great Famine, led to the Easter Rising, a war of independence and the Irish Free State in 1922.
dyk: Ireland’s population fell from about 8.2 million in 1841 to about 4.4 million in 1911 through famine deaths and emigration, while Great Britain’s more than doubled.
ev: The union of Great Britain and Ireland takes effect on 1 January
Nelson defeats the French and Spanish fleets at Trafalgar
Wellington and Blücher defeat Napoleon at Waterloo
The Great Reform Act widens the franchise
The Great Famine begins in Ireland
The Great Exhibition opens at the Crystal Palace in London
The Irish Free State is established; Northern Ireland stays in the UK

f.founder: William Pitt the Younger (Acts of Union, 1800)
f.predecessor: Kingdom of Great Britain; Kingdom of Ireland
f.successor: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland; Irish Free State
